content: Before initiating oral microbiota therapy, it is essential to complete any ongoing antibiotic regimens 2 to 4 days in advance. Oral microbiota products contain bacterial spores, and their efficacy may be reduced if co-administered with antibacterial agents due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Therefore, it is recommended to avoid or use alternative drugs when possible. Specific antibiotics, such as methenamine, metronidazole, minocycline, moxifloxacin, nafcillin, neomycin, nitrofurantoin, norfloxacin, ofloxacin, omadacycline, oritavancin, oxacillin, penicillin G (aqueous, benzathine, or procaine), penicillin VK, piperacillin, plazomicin, polymyxin B, quinupristin/dalfopristin, relebactam, retapamulin, rifamycin, rifaximin, sarecycline, streptomycin, sulbactam/durlobactam, sulfadiazine, sulfanilamide, sulfisoxazole, sulopenem, tebipenem, tedizolid, telavancin, tetracycline, tigecycline, tobramycin, trimethoprim, and vancomycin, are known to decrease the effectiveness of oral microbiota therapy. These interactions occur due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, and alternative treatments should be considered. Oral microbiota therapy is a live biotherapeutic product designed to deliver a diverse consortium of microbes to the gut, primarily to reduce recurrent Clostridioides difficile infections following antibiotic treatment. Each dose, typically consisting of four capsules, should be taken on an empty stomach before the first meal of the day. The product should be stored in its original packaging at temperatures between 2°C and 25°C (36°F to 77°F) and should not be frozen. There is no available data on the use of oral microbiota therapy in pregnant women, and developmental toxicity studies in animals have not been conducted. It is also unknown whether the product is excreted in human milk or its effects on breastfed infants and milk production. For pregnant women, the safety profile is generally acceptable, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. This information is provided for general educational purposes. Formulary status and drug interactions may vary, and it is recommended to consult the applicable plan provider for the most current information.
